TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
In which country is British Aerospace 146?
British Aerospace 146: United Kingdom. Production figures include the Avro RJ, an improved version from Avro International Aerospace, a subsidiary of BAE Systems.
Who is credited with discovering Fructose?
Fructose: Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut. Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
Who is credited with discovering LSD?
LSD: Albert Hofmann. LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
Who is credited with discovering Manganese?
Manganese: Johan Gottlieb Gahn. Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.

Despite resembling an unrelated shrub in leaf and flower shape, this shade-loving carrot-family plant has spread worldwide as an invasive garden escapee since being introduced as an ornamental — what is it?
Aegopodium podagraria is a species of flowering plant in the carrot family Apiaceae that grows in shady places.
Endemic to the rainforests of Sumatra, this plant grows an enormous inflorescence that blooms only rarely and briefly, emitting the stench of rotting flesh to lure pollinators — what plant is it?
Amorphophallus titanum is a flowering plant in the family Araceae.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
This fig species develops extra trunks from its own aerial prop roots, letting a single tree spread outward seemingly forever, one variety is even the national tree of India. Name it?
Banyan is a fig that develops accessory trunks from adjacent prop roots, allowing the tree to spread outwards indefinitely.
This colourless industrial compound, easily dissolved in organic solvents but not water, is the key ingredient in most polycarbonate plastics — which chemical?
Bisphenol A (BPA) is a chemical compound primarily used in the manufacturing of various plastics.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy and a prodrug of morphine, which opiate treats mild-to-moderate pain and is often paired with paracetamol?
Codeine is an opiate and prodrug of morphine mainly used to treat pain, coughing, and diarrhea.
This is the capacity to produce novel, valuable ideas or works — whether an invention, a scientific theory, a joke, or a piece of jewelry — through the exercise of imagination — what's the capacity?
Creativity is the ability to generate novel and valuable ideas or works through the exercise of imagination.
With interlocking neck vertebrae that prevent almost any head movement, which genus of prehensile-tailed marsupials is commonly called the large American opossums?
Didelphis is a genus of New World marsupials.
Born in North Carolina in 1983, this former NSA contractor leaked classified files exposing global surveillance programs after working for the CIA, Dell, and a defense contractor — name him?

Edward Snowden (born June 21, 1983) is a former United States National Security Agency (NSA) intelligence contractor who leaked classified documents revealing the existence of global surveillance programs.
Co-founder of MIT's J-PAL poverty lab, she shared a 2019 Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for using randomized trials against global poverty — who is it?

Esther Duflo (born 25 October 1972) is a French-American economist currently serving as the Abdul Latif Jameel Professor of Poverty Alleviation and Development Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

In English its plural is the same word for many individuals but changes form when you mean many species — a quirk of this gill-bearing, cold-blooded vertebrate that lacks limbs with digits. What is it?
Fish is an aquatic, anamniotic, gill-bearing vertebrate animal with a tough cranium to protect the brain, but lacking limbs with digits.
Native to Pacific coastal waters from Alaska to Baja California, this giant burrowing clam can grow a siphon over three feet long and live for more than a century — which creature?
Geoduck (Panopea generosa) is a species of very large saltwater clam in the family Hiatellidae.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".
Honored across Asia as a model healer and "Medicine King," this 5th-century BCE physician of Rajgir tended to King Bimbisāra — and to the Buddha himself. Who was he?
Jīvaka was the personal physician of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisra.

Amphoteric and unreactive, this post-transition metal reacts with both acids and bases, melts at a low temperature, and tarnishes from shiny to dull gray in air — and three of its isotopes end major nuclear decay chains. Which element is it?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.

Featuring a distinctive twin-boom design with a central pod housing the cockpit and guns, this American World War II fighter aircraft also served as a night fighter and long-range escort when fitted with drop tanks — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.
A sugar alcohol used both as a low-calorie sweetener and as a medication to reduce eye and brain pressure. It's poorly absorbed by the intestines. What's the name of this compound?
Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication. It is unclear if use is safe in pregnancy.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
Containing antimicrobial lysozymes and immunoglobulins, most of this protective body fluid is produced in the gastrointestinal tract — what is it called?
Mucus is a slippery fluid produced by, and covering, mucous membranes.
Also called niacin, this organic compound is an essential vitamin B3 that plants and animals produce from the amino acid tryptophan. What is it?
Nicotinic acid is an organic compound and a vitamer of vitamin B3, an essential human nutrient.

Sitting in life's hierarchy between tissue and a full body system, this term describes a group of different tissues — like the epithelial and muscle layers of the gut wall — joined to serve one shared function. What is it?
Organ (biology) is a collection of tissues joined in a structural unit to serve a common function.

The males of this Phasianidae bird are famed for piercing calls and extravagant plumage; its Asiatic species include blue, green, and a third found only in the Congo Basin — what is this bird, collectively?

Peafowl is a common name for two bird species of the genus Pavo and one species of the closely related genus Afropavo within the tribe Pavonini of the family Phasianidae (the pheasants and their allies).

Enclosed in a papery husk formed from its calyx, the fruit of this nightshade-family genus tastes like a firm tomato crossed with a sweet, tangy grape — nearly half of its species grow only in Mexico. Name the genus?
Physalis (from Ancient) is a genus of approximately 75 to 90 flowering plants in the nightshade family (Solanaceae), which are native to the Americas and Australasia.
Element number 19, this silvery alkali metal reacts so eagerly with air that it forms flaky white peroxide within seconds — and its symbol K comes from the Neo-Latin word kalium. What is it?
Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes includes some of the world's largest and kills by coiling to suffocate rather than by injecting venom — what is the family called?

Pythonidae are a family of nonvenomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
This spiny thistle species has distinctive red-to-purple flowers and shiny, pale green mottled leaves, and is a fairly typical member of the daisy family — what plant is it?
Silybum marianum is a species of thistle.
This Polish-American Manhattan Project mathematician dreamed up the Monte Carlo method, the cellular automaton, and the design behind thermonuclear weapons — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam (13 April 1909 - 13 May 1984) was a Polish and, later an American mathematician who made important contributions in advancing the understanding of nuclear physics and computer science.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
This viral brain infection, transmitted through the bite of infected parasitic arachnids, saw its European case count climb almost 400% over three decades. What is this arachnid-spread illness?
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
Belonging mostly to one family of long-snouted beetles, this group includes bark beetles and grain-damaging pests despite some members lacking the trademark snout — what are they?
Weevil are beetles belonging to the superfamily Curculionoidea, known for their very long snouts.
Discovered in 1807 and named for the Roman goddess of home and hearth, this is thought to be the second-largest asteroid and the only known rocky protoplanet still intact in the belt — which one?
4 Vesta: Second largest main-belt asteroid. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Native to sub-Saharan grasslands and woodlands, this animal is the largest living land species, with the largest recorded specimen standing nearly 13 feet tall at the shoulder — which species is it?
African bush elephant: Species of mammal. Its skin is grey with scanty hairs, and bending cracks which support thermoregulation by retaining water.

Its seasonal form is called hay fever: a type I hypersensitivity reaction where the immune system overreacts to airborne allergens, bringing sneezing, a runny nose, and itchy, watery eyes — what's the medical name?
Allergic rhinitis: Nasal inflammation due to allergens in the air.
This scientific discipline uses techniques from titration to mass spectrometry to identify unknown compounds and measure exactly how much of each substance is present in a mixture - which field?
Analytical chemistry: Study of the separation, identification, and quantification of matter.
This psychological state describes a lack of feeling, motivation, or concern, sitting on a spectrum between normal drive and akinetic mutism — what is it called?
Apathy: State of indifference, or the suppression of emotions.
First described in 1740 under the name Compositae, this enormous flowering-plant family includes daisies, asters and sunflowers — what is it?
Asteraceae: Large family of flowering plants.
A sessile marine arthropod related to crabs and lobsters, folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety of it — what creature is it?
Barnacle: Subclass of sessile marine crustaceans.
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Built as a militarized derivative of a popular 737 airliner, this maritime patrol aircraft hunts submarines for the US Navy and allies like India, Australia and the UK — which aircraft?
Boeing P-8 Poseidon: American maritime patrol aircraft. The Boeing P-8 Poseidon is an American maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft developed and produced by Boeing Defense, Space & Security.

Characterized by cycles of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors like self-induced vomiting, this eating disorder has an estimated genetic risk factor between 30 and 80 percent — what is it called?
Bulimia nervosa: Eating disorder. Bulimia is more common among those who have a close relative with the condition.
Also known as hemp when grown for fiber rather than its psychoactive use, this Asian-native plant genus includes up to three disputed species — which plant?
Also known as an Ovcharka, this large livestock-guardian breed was developed in the Soviet Union around 1920 from mountain and steppe animals of the Caucasus region — which breed?
Caucasian Shepherd Dog: Russian breed of livestock guardian dog. It was bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.
Covered in coarse black hair but bare-faced, this great ape is humans' closest living relative according to fossil and DNA evidence, and lives in groups of up to 150 — which species?
Chimpanzee: Species of great ape. The chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
This genus of some 100 low-growing perennials gives us saffron from the dried stigmas of one autumn-blooming species — name the flower genus?
This basic unit of time — averaging 24 hours, or 86,400 seconds — marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun, and got split into weeks, months, and years. What is it?
Day: Time of one rotation around a planet axis.

Governed since 1961 by the Vienna Convention, this practice of using official representatives to influence international relations became a professionalized field in the early 20th century. What is it?
Diplomacy: Practice of conducting negotiations between representatives of groups or states.
This condition involves involuntarily repeating words or sounds spoken by someone else, and is commonly seen in autism, ADHD, and Tourette syndrome. What is it called?
This branch of zoology, whose name derives from Greek words for 'insect' and 'study,' covers a field that has described over 1.3 million species — which discipline?
The only Old World member of its family to breed in the Northern Hemisphere's temperate zones, this migratory songbird winters in central and southern Africa — what is it?
Eurasian golden oriole: Species of bird.
This Swiss thinker, alongside Charles Sanders Peirce, is considered one of the two founders of semiotics — the field he himself called 'semiology' — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure: Swiss linguist and philosopher (1857–1913)
Part of the rose family and prized for fruit that ranges from very sweet to notably tart, this genus's garden hybrid is an important commercial crop worldwide — which genus is it?
One of Maxwell's equations, this application of the divergence theorem connects electric charge distribution to the electric field it creates. Which one is it?
Gauss's law: Foundational law of electromagnetism relating electric field and charge distributions.
Brought to market by Monsanto in 1974 under the brand name Roundup, this herbicide works by blocking a key enzyme that plants need to grow — what is it?
Glyphosate: Systemic herbicide and crop desiccant.
A founder of psychophysics, this German scientist captured how sensation relates to stimulus in a logarithmic law that now bears his and Weber's names — who was he?
Gustav Fechner: German experimental psychologist, physicist, and philosopher (1801–1887)

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?
This condition describes a shortage of oxygen at the tissue level rather than in the blood itself, and can occur normally during intense exercise — what is it?
Hypoxia (medicine): Medical condition of lack of oxygen in the tissues.

A functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel movement consistency over long periods, sometimes years, it can negatively affect quality of life and is associated with anxiety and depression. What condition is this?
Irritable bowel syndrome: Functional gastrointestinal disorder. The cause of IBS is not known but multiple factors have been proposed to lead to the condition.
Despite its name, this is actually a species of sunflower native to central North America, grown across temperate zones for its edible tuber — also called a sunchoke. What is it?
Jerusalem artichoke: Species of sunflower native to eastern North America. It is cultivated widely across the temperate zone for its tuber, which is used as a root vegetable.
Developed for the Soviet Navy and known to NATO by a code name, this helicopter remains in service with several countries including Russia, Ukraine, and India -- which aircraft?
With a toothed, funnel-like sucking mouth, this jawless fish's name may derive from Latin for 'stone licker,' and it's genetically closer to hagfish than to any jawed vertebrate — what is it?
Lamprey: Class of jawless fish. Lampreys (sometimes inaccurately called lamprey eels) are a group of jawless fish composing the order Petromyzontiformes, sole order in the class Petromyzontida.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
Originating in 1993 and written in ANSI C, this lightweight scripting language was designed to be embedded inside other applications — which language?
Lua: Lightweight programming language. Lua is a lightweight, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language designed mainly for embedded use in applications.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Its name means 'big tooth,' and this extinct giant mackerel shark — once mistaken for a great white relative — is known only from fragmentary remains. What is it?
Megalodon: Extinct giant shark species. Megalodon probably had a major impact on the structure of marine communities.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?

Dropped from a B-52 and boosted by a modified Pegasus rocket stage before its own scramjet took over, this experimental hypersonic craft still holds the record for fastest jet-powered flight at about Mach 9.6 — what is it?
NASA X-43: Unmanned US experimental hypersonic aircraft, 1991-2000.

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
A Boston physician, medical reformer, and 'fireside' poet, this polymath delighted readers with his 'Breakfast-Table' series begun in 1858. Who was he?
Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.: American poet, essayist, physician (1809–1894)
With long dense grey fur and rounded ears set oddly low on the sides of its head, this small wild cat — first described in 1776 near Lake Baikal — roams the cold steppes of Central Asia. What is it?
Pallas's cat: Species of small wild cat. Pallas's cat (Otocolobus manul), also called manul, is a small wild cat with long and dense light grey fur, and rounded ears set low on the sides of the head.

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Sitting less than a degree from the north celestial pole, this yellow supergiant is famously steady for navigation — but is secretly a triple star system. What is it?
Polaris: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor.

Built from long chains of amino acid residues, these biomolecules fold into specific 3D shapes that catalyze reactions, copy DNA, and ferry molecules around the cell. What are these workhorse macromolecules?
Protein: Biomolecule consisting of chains of amino acid residues.
The sole member of its genus and a relative of apples and pears, this hard, aromatic golden fruit is too tart to enjoy raw but turns lovely as jam or a fragrant cheese — what is it?
With the widest geographic range of any non-human primate, this brown-to-grey Old World monkey lives in matrilineal troops of up to 200 individuals — which species?
Rhesus macaque: Species of Old World monkey. The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.
What term describes herbivorous mammals like cattle and giraffes that digest plant matter by regurgitating and re-chewing it as cud?
Ruminant: Hoofed herbivorous grazing or browsing mammals.
About 90% of cases trace to a herniated spinal disc pressing on a nerve root, producing a shooting pain that runs from the lower back down one leg — what's the condition?
Sciatica: Lower-back pain that can extend down the leg.
Called the 'father of modern differential geometry,' this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet was honored with a medal the IMU named after him in 2010 — who is he?

Shiing-Shen Chern: Chinese-American mathematician and poet. Shiing-Shen Chern (Chinese: 陳省身; pinyin: Chén Xǐngshēn; October 26, 1911 – December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Native to Eurasia and found in Paleolithic-era deposits in ancient Britain, this flowering plant's ripe berries and cooked leaves are eaten in some regions despite its nightshade family's fearsome reputation — what is it?
Solanum nigrum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The plant was known and mentioned by ancient herbalists, including Dioscorides.
Known by the Reddit username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded the platform and also launched the now-defunct airfare search engine Hipmunk — who is he?
Steve Huffman: American web developer and entrepreneur (born 1983)
Serving as prime minister of Turkey seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, he was also the first PM to have been born in the Turkish Republic — who was he?

Süleyman Demirel: President of Turkey from 1993 to 2000. Demirel was the leader of the opposition from 1971 to 1975 before forming a right-wing government known as the First Nationalist Front, which collapsed in 1977.
This large mass of gray matter sits between the cerebral cortex and the midbrain, relaying sensory and motor signals to the cortex while regulating sleep and alertness — what is this brain structure?
Thalamus: Structure within the brain. It has several functions, such as the relaying of sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex and the regulation of consciousness, sleep, and alertness.
This colorless solvent's sweet smell partly explains the aroma of gasoline and paint fumes, and its IUPAC name is simply methylbenzene — which aromatic hydrocarbon is it?
Toluene: Aromatic hydrocarbon. Toluene is a colorless, water-insoluble liquid with a sweet smell, and is partially responsible for the aroma of gasoline and paint fumes.
First flown in 1952, this nuclear-capable Soviet bomber is the only turboprop strategic bomber still flying — its contra-rotating propellers earning it the NATO nickname 'Bear.' What is it?
Tupolev Tu-95: Russian strategic bomber aircraft.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.

In general relativity, this hypothetical region of spacetime is considered the theoretical mirror image of a much better-known cosmic trap — nothing can enter it, though light, matter, and energy may escape. What is this region called?
White hole: Hypothetical object of spacetime. In this sense, it is the opposite of a black hole, from which energy, matter, light and information cannot escape.
Sold under the brand name Ambien, which nonbenzodiazepine 'Z-drug' cuts the time to fall asleep by about fifteen minutes?
The symbol for scandium is Sc. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
The symbol for hydrogen is H. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
